lines: 1 package is imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 795,563 B in 128 modules, 15.5 % of the static path of calendar-main.js, imported by its root in 88 files: components/AppNavigation/AppNavigationHeader/AppNavigationHeaderDatePicker.vue (NcButton, NcDateTimePicker), components/AppNavigation/AppNavigationHeader/AppNavigationHeaderNewEvent.vue (NcButton), and 86 more. It is imported per module as well, through 22 other specifiers.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

17 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 16,422 B, 0.3 % of the static path of calendar-main.js, next to 47 components the source names and 13 those pull in.

These arrive through the root import, and @nextcloud/calendar-availability-vue on the same page imports the root as well: as long as one module imports the barrel, the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports in the app drop nothing while that package does; the specifier to change is in @nextcloud/calendar-availability-vue.
